The **bug**: that routine applied the minimum-image correction **independently to every bond**. That is only self-consistent when a molecule fits within half the cell. For a molecule that spans a larger fraction of the box the per-bond constraints over-determine the atom positions, and the algorithm tears the molecule apart — here it slammed CB onto a copy one cell away, producing bonds of ~1.17 nm. That's the "locally implausible molecular dimensions" observation (the diagnostic's `maximum` bond was **1.1738 nm**).

## Repair

I replaced the per-bond re-imaging in `make_whole` with a **bond-graph traversal (BFS)**: for each connected component it places every atom into the same periodic image as its bonded traversal parent. A single rigid copy of each molecule is therefore kept whole; the minimum-image offset is only ever applied to a single (short, well-defined) covalent bond. The adjacency list is built in **CSR** form (O(n_atoms + n_bonds) memory) so it scales to large systems.

This is a **general** fix — it is molecule- and file-agnostic, preserves the public API, coordinate units (nm), and input semantics.
